t.E472f.agn: In 2020 EFSA set an ADI based on the group ADI of 240 mg/kg body weight, expressed as tartaric acid, and found no safety concern at the reported use levels. In its 2025 follow-up opinion EFSA cited an ADI of 600 mg/kg body weight for this additive and stated that estimated intake remained below this value.
t.E472f.body: During digestion in the body it is largely broken down into glycerol, fatty acids and the corresponding organic acids (acetic and tartaric acid); these are used like the fats in foods.
t.E472f.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E472f.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by esterification of mono- and diglycerides with tartaric acid and acetic acid (or their anhydrides).
t.E472f.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI set based on the tartaric acid group ADI (240 mg/kg body weight per day), no safety concern.
t.E472f.regx.1: Follow-up opinion: ADI of 600 mg/kg body weight per day; estimated intake below the ADI. Insufficient technical data submitted for a change to the specifications.
t.E472f.summary: An emulsifier derived from mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids. It improves texture in bread, cake and margarine; the fat source may be vegetable or animal.
t.E472f.what: As an emulsifier, it improves the structure and consistency of dough.
